A finding is work, as a ready card is: the wake has work when `ready_cards` or `sweep_findings` is not empty. `wakes_since_last_session` counts the wakes after the newest of those runs that started no session, refused before they started or skipped by Jev on purpose; such a wake is not a failure. Each run's `outcome` says what happened: `session ended cleanly`, `session failed (...)` or `session still running` describe a session; when a card needed the human in that session, `needed_human` lists its decisions, and a non-null `answered_at` means the human has answered since, so that blocker is resolved. Each run also has `status`, `summary` and the session `result`.

size-bounded-investigation.recorded: live call to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone at 2026-09-27T12:25:39Z, request and reply verbatim

criteria.m: The hardest decision is hard: the goal must be interpreted, an architecture chosen between real alternatives, or a cause found that could lie in any of several parts of the system -- an intermittent failure, a race, a problem nobody can yet explain -- before anything is built. Work that needs the largest model, and still one deliverable that one worker finishes in one turn.
criteria.s: Most work: decisions inside a clear goal. New behaviour -- a command, a validation rule, a function or a whole module -- whose edge cases, error handling, refusals or output shape the worker decides; a change across several files with design choices; or a bounded search, a fix or a question whose cause or answer lies in one place or among a few named candidates.
criteria.split: Larger than `m`: the goal needs more than one worker turn, however easy or hard each part is. It bundles several independent deliverables -- different commands, screens, installers or subsystems that could each be their own pull request -- or rewrites many parts of the system at once, or its `test` needs several separate setups. The orchestrator splits such a card into children and sizes each of them.
criteria.xs: Really small and straightforward: the goal names the exact edit, a few lines, fully specified, with nothing to decide and nothing to find out -- a typo, a changed constant, a rename, a moved file. Never new behaviour: a new command, check or refusal is at least `s`.

size:sys-d9.instructions: How much effort and complexity is in `cards.sys-d9`: `xs`, `s`, `m`, or `split`? The size fixes the worker: the model and reasoning effort that work the card follow from it. The human's rule for every tier: "delegate to capable orchestrators and workers; do not cheap out on their capabilities, do not underestimate the tasks, do not overestimate what the agents can do, and do not overspend." Size measures the hardest decision inside the goal and how clear the goal is, not how big the change is: a one-line fix whose cause must first be found is `s` or `m`. `split` is not a degree of difficulty: it means the card is larger than `m`, more than one worker finishes in one turn (one Claude Code session in one worktree, one pull request), so the orchestrator splits it first; a card that is one deliverable, however hard, is `xs`, `s` or `m`. Read its `goal`, `limits` and `test`.

sys-d9.goal: Find out whether a headless run can read remaining subscription usage (status-line `rate_limits`, the stream-json rate-limit event, or nothing); write the evidence and a recommendation in the card's notes and report the choice for the human
sys-d9.test: The card's notes carry the evidence and a recommendation; no code merged
sys-d9.title: usage-limit signal spike
